title: Introduce a breaking API without confusing software and API versions
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Distinguish software and API versions; an incompatible endpoint switch must not count as safe migration.
exactSourceBehavior: Use versioned endpoints or transitional adapters instead of abruptly changing a live contract.
exactParentAcceptance: A stable compatible route can migrate all consumers; a breaking API cannot be force-rerouted and declared uninterrupted.
preconditions: Standalone modern browser with local JavaScript enabled; no server or account.
Three synthetic consumers initially require API v1; blue software 1.8.0 serves v1.
Green software 2.0.0 uses API v2 internally; the old v1 shape can be retained through a transitional adapter.
Explicit pre-attempt client upgrades change declared contracts; selecting software does not.
actions: Independently choose software destination, stable-adapter/versioned/force-v2 route, explicit client upgrades and observation coverage.
Run one bounded cutover attempt and inspect per-consumer contract, response shape and software identity.
Compare failed, unknown and successful synthetic migration outcomes without erasing previous attempts.
Operate by keyboard and explicitly reset to the original fixture.
syntheticInputAndTrace: model.js; three fixed synthetic profile journeys per attempt; API paths and HTTP statuses are data, not requests.
expectedAssertions: Stable transitional adapter and consumer-versioned endpoints can migrate mixed v1/v2 consumers to green with their declared shapes preserved.
HTTP 200 from a forced v2 endpoint fails v1 consumers; interrupted journeys remain in the denominator.
Only explicit complete client upgrades permit all consumers to use the breaking endpoint without an adapter.
Successful blue requests have zero migration credit; missing started observations remain unknown.
Strict exact-enum, state/history and six-attempt guards reject forged or over-limit operations without mutation.
History retains earlier failed attempts; keyboard, validation, explicit reset and restrictive CSP work in an actual browser.

bounds.history: Memory only; cleared only by explicit reset or page reload.

iac.sequence: After complete loadable-stub assertion RED; before behavioral implementation.
iac.reason: No resources are created; cloud/IaC/identity/scaffolding/deployment/spend are not authorized.

testRuntime.lifecycle: openIsolatedLesson with awaited close in finally; abandoned lifecycle prototype is unqualified.

limits: Synthetic contract/response/deployment observations only; no HTTP protocol or real adapter proof.
No native Azure, Node.js 24 production, source-parent completion or five-nines certification.
B-S053, D-S053 and source prerequisites D-S051/D-S052 remain separate.
No identity, authentication, accounts, tokens, keys or credentials are relevant or modeled.
No cloud, IaC, scaffold, identity registration, deployment, expenditure, downloads, packages, framework, root/shared edits or foreground leases.
One frozen S unit only; tests, plumbing, evidence and refinement receive no additional credit.
